why: Rhenium is recovered from the roaster flue dust of molybdenum concentrate, so the two metals leave the same plants.
condition: Rhenium recovery stays tied to molybdenum roasting rather than dedicated circuits.
falsifier: Rhenium supply decouples from molybdenum throughput.

why: Refining catalysts and superalloys draw the same nickel units, so demand strength on one side tightens the other.
condition: Both sides buy nickel at index-linked prices.
falsifier: One side is fully hedged or substitutes away.

why: Transformer and cable windings are a first-order copper demand line into the same mine and smelter stack.
condition: Grid and data center buildout remains copper intensive.
falsifier: Aluminium substitution takes the winding share.

why: Furnace graphite and battery anodes compete for the same high purity graphite capacity and the same export licence regime.
condition: Chinese export policy treats both products comparably.
falsifier: Licences separate the two product lines.

why: Hafnium is the twin of zirconium in the same separation step, so nuclear cladding and blade coatings share a feed.
condition: Zirconium and hafnium continue to be split at the same plants.
falsifier: Cladding moves to alternative materials.

why: SF6 and HFO refrigerants both start from fluorspar and hydrofluoric acid, so one mineral chain feeds both nodes.
condition: Fluorine chemistry remains the route for both products.
falsifier: Alternative chemistries displace one side.

why: Semiconductor crucibles and optical fiber preforms draw on the same high purity silica deposits.
condition: Both industries keep needing the same grade of silica.
falsifier: Synthetic silica displaces natural quartz on one side.

why: Crystal growth, fiber drawing and fab processes share the rare gas supply.
condition: Helium and rare gas supply stays tight.
falsifier: Recovery projects loosen the market.

why: Battery foil is another copper demand line competing for cathode supply.
condition: Foil demand grows with storage deployment.
falsifier: Alternative current collectors take share.

why: Catalyst and magnet rare earths come from the same separation lines, so demand from one raises cost for the other.
condition: La and Ce separation capacity is shared with the heavy rare earth circuits.
falsifier: Dedicated catalyst grade lines absorb the demand.

why: Skilled trades and foundry labour compete for the same apprenticeship pool.
condition: Both sectors hire from the same training pipeline.
falsifier: Programmes expand to cover both.

why: The cooling load node is a sub-mechanism of the data center site node, written at its own resolution.
condition: Cooling load remains a material share of site engineering.
falsifier: Cooling becomes a minor design line.

why: Firm nuclear capacity is contracted directly by data center operators.
condition: Behind the meter and PPA structures keep growing.
falsifier: Operators return to grid supply only.

why: Molybdenum is a byproduct of porphyry copper mines, so the catalyst input hangs off the copper node.
condition: Byproduct recovery stays economical.
falsifier: Molybdenum becomes a primary mining product.

why: The dig is the resolution beneath the anchor node.
condition: The anchor node remains the mechanism of record.
falsifier: The dig contradicts the anchor and the anchor is updated.

why: Turbine slots are a concrete case of the capacity constraint mechanism.
condition: Capacity constraint remains the governing mechanism.
falsifier: Another bottleneck explains the same slips.

why: Interregional transfer sits inside the interconnection bottleneck.
condition: Transfer additions remain gated by the bottleneck.
falsifier: Transfer capacity expands freely.

why: Storage is flexible capacity inside the constraint mechanism.
condition: Storage remains the marginal flexible resource.
falsifier: Other flexibility dominates.

why: Power electronics gate converter and inverter delivery.
condition: Semiconductors remain on the critical path.
falsifier: Inventories cover project schedules durably.

why: Magnet makers are the expression layer the supplier basket watches.
condition: The basket remains the traded surface.
falsifier: The expression changes instrument.

why: Cooling load growth is the force behind the cooling bottleneck.
condition: Density growth continues.
falsifier: Cooling stops binding site schedules.

why: Switchgear shares the critical path with transformers.
condition: Both remain gated by the same equipment complex.
falsifier: Switchgear lead times decouple from transformer lead times.

why: Interconnect is a sub-node of the data center site.
condition: Compute growth keeps pulling fiber.
falsifier: Compute stops needing new interconnect.

why: Crews are the concrete form of the labor bottleneck.
condition: Labour remains a binding constraint in the regions of the buildout.
falsifier: Crew supply clears and equipment becomes the only constraint.

why: Grid and data center copper is a demand line inside the copper factor.
condition: The factor remains the market reference.
falsifier: Contract structures decouple physical from factor.

why: Firm power additions are a capacity constraint case.
condition: Firm power remains the binding commitment for load growth.
falsifier: Firm obligations loosen.

why: Catalyst supply is a materials constraint case under the same mechanism.
condition: Catalyst supply remains a material constraint for refiners.
falsifier: Catalyst is never supply constrained.

why: Compute buildout contracts firm power, so committed power capacity is the resource it competes for.
condition: Firm capacity remains the product operators contract for.
falsifier: Operators build their own generation entirely.

why: Workload demand growth is the origin of the load growth utilities now plan against.
condition: Workload growth continues to convert into electricity demand.
falsifier: Efficiency decouples workload from power.

why: Provider inventory state is the fastest observable marker of which phase the compute cycle is in.
condition: Listed prices and availability reflect inventory.
falsifier: Prices are policy artifacts decoupled from utilisation.

why: Firm capacity procurement competes with nuclear PPAs for the same load contracts.
condition: Nuclear remains a contracted firm source.
falsifier: Nuclear capacity is allocated outside the market.

why: New firm capacity in most markets means new gas turbines.
condition: Turbines remain the marginal firm capacity technology.
falsifier: Storage or imports satisfy firm obligations.

why: Special contracts allocate the cost of serving dense compute and its cooling load.
condition: Large load tariffs remain the allocation mechanism.
falsifier: Standard tariffs absorb the cost.

why: Approved transmission projects consume the same transformer supply as generation projects.
condition: Transmission and generation compete for the same equipment.
falsifier: Transmission uses distinct equipment classes.

why: Transformer scarcity during the current buildout repeats the equipment bottleneck pattern of prior cycle phase twos.
condition: Equipment bottlenecks recur in buildout phases.
falsifier: Equipment supply keeps pace this time.

why: Idle interconnection capacity is the dark fiber of this cycle: built, unused, and cheap for the second wave.
condition: Interconnection capacity can be re-used by later projects.
falsifier: Queue capacity is consumed immediately on award.

why: The second wave converts infrastructure into regulated, contracted ownership, the transmission owner's structure.
condition: Regulated ownership remains the end state.
falsifier: Political change breaks the regulated model.

why: Queue milestone posts are one of the event classes the clock starts on.
condition: Queue updates are published with usable timestamps.
falsifier: Queue updates are undated or retrospective.

why: The entry window is measured through post-event drift and the rehearsal that delays entry.
condition: Drift survives delayed entry.
falsifier: Drift vanishes when entries are delayed.

why: Provider capex becomes the load forecast and the utility capital plan.
condition: Provider projects reach utilities as committed load.
falsifier: Projects stay behind the meter on self generation.

why: The colocation cycle is the direct prior for the data center site asset class.
condition: Site economics repeat the colocation pattern.
falsifier: AI sites have fundamentally different contracts.

why: Provider margins are the cash-flow channel the outcome node measures.
condition: Contracted revenue remains the margin driver.
falsifier: Margins are regulated to cost of service.

why: The dig is the resolution beneath the capex level outcome.
condition: The outcome remains the measured object.
falsifier: The dig contradicts the outcome construction.

why: The dig is the resolution beneath the compute rental feature.
condition: The feature remains the measured object.
falsifier: The dig contradicts the feature construction.

why: Energy providers are the expression surface the utility basket watches.
condition: The basket remains the traded surface.
falsifier: The expression moves to credit or contracts.

why: The analogue cycle machine is the temporal resolution of the capacity constraint.
condition: Capacity constraint remains the governing mechanism.
falsifier: Cycles stop repeating.

why: Entry windows are attached to the disclosure event class the manifest already names.
condition: Disclosures remain the event class.
falsifier: The edge moves to non-disclosure events.

why: HVDC cables are a step change in copper and aluminium conductor demand per kilometre, and cable makers buy against those orders.
condition: Cable orders translate into conductor demand within the same procurement window.
falsifier: Cable makers hold conductor inventory through the build cycle and orders do not reach the metal market.

why: Compute buildout and grid buildout draw on the same heavy equipment and labor pools: transformers, switchgear, turbines, crews.
condition: Both are constrained by the same equipment and labor supply, so one raises the other's cost and lead time.
falsifier: Equipment lead times and crew wages are flat while both capex lines rise.

why: Provider capex becomes depreciation, interest and contracted capacity, which is what equity prices.
condition: Capex is funded with debt or equity and its depreciation reaches reported earnings within two years.
falsifier: Capex is fully expensed against revenue with no earnings footprint, or is so contracted that it carries no market risk.

why: Token and inference volume is the demand that fills rented capacity, so it reaches provider revenue before it reaches prices.
condition: Demand growth shows up as utilisation first and revenue per megawatt second.
falsifier: Provider revenue grows while token volume is flat, or falls while token volume grows.

why: Transformer core steel and the turbine supply that serves data center power commitments come from the same electrical steel and casting capacity.
condition: The same mills and casters serve both the grid equipment and the on site power equipment.
falsifier: Data center power equipment is sourced from a supply base independent of grid transformer steel.

why: Nuclear firm power arrives with its own large transformer and switchgear demand, stacked on the same core steel supply.
condition: Nuclear restarts and new builds order grid equipment from the same supply as everything else.
falsifier: Nuclear projects source their electrical equipment outside the shared supply chain.

why: Large power transformers and SiC power devices are both conversion and control equipment on the same grid capex line, and they substitute at the margin in some applications.
condition: Both sit in the same substation and converter budgets, so their orders move together.
falsifier: Substation budgets show one rising while the other falls for reasons of technology substitution.
